newsitem.title: USA: Christopher says Mideast peace process in jeopardy.
newsitem.headline: Christopher says Mideast peace process in jeopardy.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Sunday that the eruption of violence in the Middle East last week posed a grave threat to the peace process.

"The peace process is in no doubt jeopardy," Christopher said on NBC Television's "Meet the Press" program. "This is probably the worst threat it has had with 55 or more killings amd hundreds and perhaps thousands injured."
"It is urgent that the parties get back together," Christopher said.
"We shouldn't expect miracles out of this," he added of the meeting announced earlier by President Bill Clinton between Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The two have agreed to visit Washington this week to try to end the recent Middle East violence, Clinton said at a brief news conference in the White House Rose Garden. Jordan's King Hussein and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak have also been invited.
Christopher said that the peace negotiations have proven to be resilient in the past. "This is an emergency situation now," he said.
